findings.title: No ToolSet validation on skill toolkit name
findings.problem: _parse_template_toolkits accepts any string for a template's `toolkit` field; ToolKitDetails.toolkit is a bare str with no check against the ToolSet enum, so a misspelled or retired toolkit name (e.g. a future typo of 'Azure DevOps Work Item') parses successfully instead of being rejected.
findings.impact: ToolkitService._merge_skill_toolkits merges purely by matching the toolkit string, and get_core_tools/_initialize_toolkit_tools never re-validates it, so an invalid toolkit name silently reaches the assistant's merged toolkit list and never maps to any real tool: the skill-to-toolkit auto-attach this change exists to deliver no-ops with no error or log line anywhere.
findings.recommendation: In _parse_template_toolkits, reject (and log, matching the function's existing error-handling pattern) any entry whose 'toolkit' value is not a member of {t.value for t in ToolSet}, instead of letting ToolKitDetails accept an arbitrary string.

findings.title: Toolkits overwritten with [] when parsing fails
findings.problem: On the update path, `updates['toolkits'] = _parse_template_toolkits(template)` is assigned unconditionally; _parse_template_toolkits returns [] both when a template legitimately has no toolkits and when parsing raises. Unlike the companion_files update two lines below, which only writes the key when _store_companion_files returns non-None, there is no equivalent guard for toolkits.
findings.impact: If a previously-valid template's toolkits entry ever becomes unparseable on a later deploy (bad YAML edit, a ToolKitDetails field change, etc.), the next startup's create_or_update_skill call silently replaces the existing skill's stored toolkits with an empty list, severing the skill-to-toolkit coupling this change introduces, with only a single error log line and no indication the stored value changed.
findings.recommendation: Make _parse_template_toolkits distinguish 'no toolkits' from 'parse failure' (e.g. return None on failure, like _store_companion_files), and only set updates['toolkits'] when the result is not None, preserving the existing stored value otherwise.
